name: Europe hybrid attacks
value: France blames IRGC; US soldier held in UK
summary: France blamed an IRGC unit on 9 Nov for sabotage at ~700 stores; UK held a US soldier over Russia spying on 10 Nov
state: On 9 Nov France attributed the October cyber-sabotage of refrigeration systems at about 700 retail stores to the Shahid Kaveh unit linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards; hoax bomb threats also diverted flights and reached over 6,000 Italian schools in mid-November (LRT). UK counter-terrorism police arrested a US Army soldier near Gloucester on 10 Nov on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service, in a Russia-related case (PBS, citing AP). No sabotage causing casualties or repeated multi-country shutdowns was found as of 15 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Shoppers, travellers and operators of critical services in Europe can face short disruption from cyber-sabotage, hoax threats or drone sightings. Report suspicious activity to the police; UK businesses can follow NCSC and NPSA guidance.
rubric_hit: Watch: sabotage attributed to a state (France names IRGC unit, 9 Nov); no casualties or multi-country shutdowns

sources.title: LRT — Hybrid warfare in Europe: sabotage, cyberattacks, agents at the service of rival powers

why: Sabotage, arson and drone incursions over airports and bases are how state confrontation reaches daily life in the UK and Europe.
drivers: Russia–NATO tensions, drone and cyber capabilities, proxy recruitment, elections.

rubric.alert: Repeated airport or infrastructure shutdowns across several countries, or sabotage causing casualties or a major outage.
rubric.watch: Drone incursions close an airport or military base, or a sabotage incident is attributed to a state.
rubric.normal: No significant attributed sabotage or airspace incursions in Europe this week.
